stem: (Select TWO.) Kestrel Analytics is deciding whether a resource argument written as `tags = { 3 = "prod" }` will work, and whether comparing a number to its text form with `==` will ever be treated as equal. Which two statements are correct?

choices.text: Automatic type conversion between numbers and strings also applies when comparing two values with the equality operator
A map can use a number or a boolean as one of its keys, as long as every key in that map is the same type
The keys in a map are always strings
`null == ""` evaluates to `true`, treating a null and an empty string as the same absent value
Terraform automatically converts number and bool values to strings when a string is expected

rationale: Map keys are always strings, and Terraform converts number and bool values to strings wherever a string is expected. Automatic type conversion happens for most arguments but never for the equality operator, where a number and the string of that number are not treated as equal. Map keys must be strings regardless of how consistent the key types otherwise look -- a number or boolean key isn't valid. And `null` is not the same value as an empty string: `null` represents absence, while an empty string is a real, present value, so `null == ""` is false.
